answer: The PoA ledger assigns each new agent a “ridge” reputation token whose weight grows quadratically with the total stake it locks on a “terrace” bonding curve. When an agent proposes a transaction its vote is multiplied by the square of its ridge weight, so a thousand umber‑priced Sybil identities each staking 1 token contribute only the weight of a single 31‑token stake (√1000≈31). An attacker must therefore lock at least 31 tokens per fake identity to equal one genuine node, raising the cost to 31 tokens × N instead of 1 token × N.
